headline: Models infer cell-state dynamics and regulatory networks from single-cell data
label: Single Cell Regulatory Network Modeling
summary: Generative, velocity and network models are now being benchmarked against single-cell atlases to predict fate and identify upstream regulators.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of cell-state dynamics and regulatory architecture from single-cell measurements. Several items model trajectories directly: lineage inpainting with tree-structured transformers and stochastic interpolants, flow-matching generation of developmental expression distributions in BLOOM, and bowside, which jointly infers trajectories and gene regulatory networks. Others refine RNA velocity with gene kinetics priors in JuloVelo, accelerate SCENIC-type GRN inference in flashscenic, or build metabolic network ensembles from scRNA-seq in FluxSprout. Deep Lineage and the potency-method review address lineage tracing and fate inference. Not all items share this focus. The MASH interactome study, the xNNPCD cell death screen and the Core Coefficient measure address regulator prioritization from network or perturbation data. What is new is the coupling of generative dynamical models with lineage and biological priors, evaluated on defined benchmarks and atlases.
